_comment: Which top-level keys of a derived 1_cloud-configs/dist/build-<service>.json are FLEET-WIDE
broadcast, i.e. not owned by the service that consumes the file.
cloud-data-config-derive.ts documents its own emission contract for the generic
-- all owned by that one service -- plus 'services', described there as the
'cross-service registry map (every peer's ip/ports/vm/api/mcp)'. That last block is
identical broadcast traffic: it changes whenever ANY peer anywhere in the fleet changes
its address, port, domain or MCP metadata.
Consequence when change detection ignores the distinction: registering two unrelated MCP
endpoints (commit 96e362760, 2026-09-05) rewrote 115 build-*.json files, of which 104
differed in NOTHING but this registry. The detect step read 'the file changed' as 'the
service changed' and redeployed 43 services on oci-apps -- including cloud-ide
(user-prod_code-server), whose compose.nix never reads the registry.
This list lives in data because the derive step is free to add another fleet-wide block;
when it does, the only edit needed is here, not in the ship engine.
